data.content_ref: inline:The target's central error-orthogonality criterion is self-defeating relative to its own mechanism. The mechanism argues the checklist is a lossy linear projection that cannot recover the nonlinear boundary information the expert uses, so panel errors should arise from the discarded dimensions. But if the expert's errors occur at those same nonlinear boundary regions, the panel's lossy projection cannot represent them, so panel errors are driven by coarse linear-separability failures—orthogonal to the expert's boundary-specific errors. Thus error-orthogonality is exactly what coincidental lossy compression would produce, not evidence of independent signal capture. The covering principle the target appeals to (orthogonal errors ⇒ genuine independent signal) fails to distinguish genuine gain from the very lossy-compression failure it identifies as the core problem. Moreover, error-orthogonality can also arise when a simpler valid heuristic happens to track the outcome through a different feature subset than the expert uses, which is still mere checklist compliance with the right answer rather than reconstructed expert reasoning.
